title: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal/Hide answer shows reference + speaker

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I think he is right.
exercises.german: Ich glaube, dass er recht hat.
exercises.why: glauben takes a verb-final dass-clause: the two-part verb hat sits at the end, the subject er comes first.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It is important that you arrive on time.
exercises.german: Es ist wichtig, dass du pünktlich kommst.
exercises.why: The impersonal frame Es ist wichtig, dass is followed by a dass-clause with the verb kommst at the very end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I hope you feel better soon.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass du dich bald besser fühlst.
exercises.why: A verb of opinion (hoffen) allows only the complement clause, not an Infinitiv; fühlst is verb-final.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It seems nobody noticed anything.
exercises.german: Es scheint, dass niemand etwas bemerkt hat.
exercises.why: scheinen introduces a dass-clause; the perfect form bemerkt hat closes the clause in verbal-final position.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: Do you think she will come to the party?
exercises.german: Glaubst du, dass sie zur Feier kommen wird?
exercises.why: In a question the conjugated glaubst is also verb-final, and the dass-clause adds a second verb-final slot: wird.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I am convinced that this is the right decision.
exercises.german: Ich bin überzeugt, dass das die richtige Entscheidung ist.
exercises.why: The frame phrase überzeugt sein only takes a subordinate clause, never a preposition with a noun, so the final slot is ist.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It is necessary that we book earlier.
exercises.german: Es ist notwendig, dass wir früher buchen.
exercises.why: Es ist …, dass is the classic impersonal assessment clause; buchen closes it, and the subject wir sits in front of the verb.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I heard that the flight was delayed.
exercises.german: Ich habe gehört, dass der Flug verspätet war.
exercises.why: A perception verb (gehört haben) triggers a dass-clause with the perfect passive Verspätet war in final position.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It is doubtful that he will agree.
exercises.german: Es ist zweifelhaft, dass er zustimmt.
exercises.why: The expression Es ist zweifelhaft, dass judges the coming clause; the modal zustimmt ends it.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: She complained that the noise was unbearable.
exercises.german: Sie beschwerte sich, dass der Lärm unerträglich war.
exercises.why: sich beschweren über + accusative can be replaced by a dass-clause, which then has to end in war.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It bothers me that nobody tells me the truth.
exercises.german: Es stört mich, dass mir niemand die Wahrheit sagt.
exercises.why: The impersonal subject es is replaced by the object mir in the main clause; inside the clause the dative object mir precedes the final verb sagt.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I did not expect the exam to be that difficult.
exercises.german: Ich hatte nicht erwartet, dass die Prüfung so schwer sein würde.
exercises.why: A verb of expectation plus the Konjunktiv II würde: the modal verb in its subordinate form closes the dass-clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It is possible that they are still waiting for us.
exercises.german: Es ist möglich, dass sie noch auf uns warten.
exercises.why: Modal of possibility in the dass-clause: the verb is warten, and the separable prefix of warten follows it as a particle.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: He admitted that he had made a mistake.
exercises.german: Er gab zu, dass er einen Fehler gemacht hatte.
exercises.why: The verb phrase zugeben, dass … uses a preterite main verb with a perfect clause, so the double infiniite form hatte is verb-final.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I find it strange that nobody said anything.
exercises.german: Ich finde es seltsam, dass niemand etwas gesagt hat.
exercises.why: The noun es is a placeholder object that falls away inside the clause; gesagt hat is the closing verbal group.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It is said that the company is being sold.
exercises.german: Es heißt, dass die Firma verkauft werden soll.
exercises.why: The passive reporting verb verkauft werden and the modal-like sollen in its final position make the clause impersonal.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I deny that I have ever seen this film.
exercises.german: Ich bestreite, dass ich diesen Film schon einmal gesehen habe.
exercises.why: bestreiten demands a dass-clause; the perfect form gesehen habe and the negation schon einmal belong to the final slot.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It annoys me that he never listens.
exercises.german: Mich ärgert, dass er nie zuhört.
exercises.why: A verbless impersonal clause (Mich ärgert, dass …) with the object mich in front; the clause ends in zuhört.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: It goes without saying that one arrives on time.
exercises.german: Es versteht sich von selbst, dass man pünktlich kommt.
exercises.why: A fixed idiom of assessment followed by a dass-clause; the impersonal man stays the subject of the final verb kommt.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: dass-clause after a frame verb
exercises.english: I am convinced the mistake lies elsewhere.
exercises.german: Ich war überzeugt, dass der Fehler woanders liegt.
exercises.why: The frame überzeugt sein allows only the clause complement; liegt as a two-part verb closes the sentence.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: I do not know whether he is coming tonight.
exercises.german: Ich weiß nicht, ob er heute Abend kommt.
exercises.why: After weiß nicht the indirect question uses ob instead of a wh-word, and the verb kommt stands at the end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Could you tell me where the station is?
exercises.german: Könnten Sie mir sagen, wo der Bahnhof ist?
exercises.why: The indirect question is introduced by wo without a correlative second conjunction; ist is the final word of the clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: She asked me whether I had already eaten.
exercises.german: Sie fragte, ob ich schon gegessen hatte.
exercises.why: A past verb of asking is followed by an ob-clause whose verb had is verb-final, not a second finite verb.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: I wonder whether they will accept the offer.
exercises.german: Ich frage mich, ob sie das Angebot annehmen.
exercises.why: The reflexive verb fragen takes the ob-clause directly, with the verb annehmen closing it.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: It depends on whether the weather is good.
exercises.german: Es hängt davon ab, ob das Wetter gut ist.
exercises.why: The preposition ab with a dependent clause forms a verb cluster abzuhängen, but the ob-clause itself keeps verb-final ist.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Tell me whether you agree with me.
exercises.german: Sag mir, ob du mit mir einverstanden bist.
exercises.why: The imperative main clause and the ob-clause contrast: the subordinate verb bist comes after einverstanden.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Nobody knows whether the shop is open.
exercises.german: Niemand weiß, ob der Laden geöffnet hat.
exercises.why: Knowledge verbs frame an ob-clause; the perfect form geöffnet hat ends it, and the subject precedes it.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: I have not decided whether to stay or to leave.
exercises.german: Ich habe noch nicht entschieden, ob ich bleibe oder gehe.
exercises.why: Two alternatives inside one ob-clause: the finite verbs bleibe and gehe follow their subjects, so the position of two verbs is still final.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: He was unsure whether she had noticed.
exercises.german: Er war unsicher, ob sie es bemerkt hatte.
exercises.why: A predicate adjective before the clause still leaves the ob-clause verb-final: bemerkt hatte.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Can you find out whether the office is still open?
exercises.german: Kannst du herausfinden, ob das Büro noch geöffnet ist?
exercises.why: herausfinden is separated in the main clause; inside the ob-clause the separable prefix of geöffnet follows the participle.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: The question is whether the plan is realistic.
exercises.german: Die Frage ist, ob der Plan realistisch ist.
exercises.why: The copula ist appears twice; in the clause it comes last, after the predicative adjective realistisch.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: I have not checked whether the tickets are still available.
exercises.german: Ich habe nicht geprüft, ob die Tickets noch verfügbar sind.
exercises.why: A perfect main clause with a passive predicate (verfügbar sind) in the verb-final position of the ob-clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Do you know whether they have already moved?
exercises.german: Weißt du, ob sie schon umgezogen sind?
exercises.why: Again two verb positions: weißt in the question, sind at the end of the ob-clause; the perfect participle is before it.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: It was unclear whether he would come at all.
exercises.german: Es war unklar, ob er überhaupt kommen würde.
exercises.why: The Konjunktiv II würde is the last element of the indirect question, keeping verb-final order.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: She wanted to know whether I would help her.
exercises.german: Sie wollte wissen, ob ich ihr helfen würde.
exercises.why: The modal helfen and the Konjunktiv II of werden form a bracket: würde as the finite element comes last.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Let us find out whether the meeting has been cancelled.
exercises.german: Finden wir heraus, ob die Sitzung abgesagt wurde.
exercises.why: A suggestion in the imperative plus a passive clause in the verb-final slot: wurde ends the sentence.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: I do not care whether he agrees or not.
exercises.german: Mir ist egal, ob er zustimmt oder nicht.
exercises.why: The impersonal mir ist egal frames the ob-clause; the negated oder nicht comes after the closing verb zustimmt.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: It is not certain whether the delivery will arrive tomorrow.
exercises.german: Es steht nicht fest, ob die Lieferung morgen kommt.
exercises.why: A fixed impersonal expression with an ob-clause; kommt is the single verb and therefore the final word.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: Nobody could say whether the ring was real.
exercises.german: Niemand konnte sagen, ob der Ring echt war.
exercises.why: The modal konnte of perception is followed by a simple past war at the end of the ob-clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: indirect question with ob
exercises.english: We still have to check whether the visa is valid.
exercises.german: Wir müssen noch prüfen, ob das Visum gültig ist.
exercises.why: Two modal frames in one sentence: müssen in the main clause, ist at the end of the ob-clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: Do not forget to close the window!
exercises.german: Vergiss nicht, das Fenster zu schließen!
exercises.why: vergessen cannot take a dass-clause, so the verb moves into an infinitive group with zu and the verb goes to the end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: He stopped smoking last year.
exercises.german: Er hörte letztes Jahr auf zu rauchen.
exercises.why: aufhören takes a zu-infinitive, never a dass-clause; the infinitive is the last element of the sentence.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: What are you planning to do tonight?
exercises.german: Was hast du vor, heute Abend zu machen?
exercises.why: vorhaben, etwas zu tun is a verb-final construction without any conjunction at all.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: She forgot to post the letter.
exercises.german: Sie hat vergessen, den Brief aufzugeben.
exercises.why: After vergessen the accusative object is placed in front of the separable prefix, which attaches to the infinitive: aufzugeben.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: We decided to travel by train.
exercises.german: Wir haben beschlossen, mit dem Zug zu fahren.
exercises.why: beschließen requires a zu-infinitive; a comma separates the main clause from the infinitive group ending in fahren.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: Try to be quiet, please.
exercises.german: Versuch bitte, leise zu sein!
exercises.why: After the imperative of versuchen the particle zu stands directly in front of the separable verb: zu sein.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: I cannot afford to eat out every week.
exercises.german: Ich kann es mir nicht leisten, jede Woche auszugehen.
exercises.why: sich leisten is followed by a zu-infinitive group, which cannot be replaced by a dass-clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: He promised to call me back.
exercises.german: Er versprach, mich anzurufen.
exercises.why: versprechen takes a zu-infinitive with the personal object placed before the prefix: mich anzurufen.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: The doctor advised me to take it easy.
exercises.german: Der Arzt empfahl mir, mich zu schonen.
exercises.why: A separable verb appears after zu: zu schonen, with the reflexive object in front of the zu.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: Stop talking nonsense!
exercises.german: Hör auf, Unsinn zu reden!
exercises.why: The negated imperative of aufhören is followed by an accusative object and the zu-infinitive reden.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: I do not feel like cooking tonight.
exercises.german: Ich habe keine Lust, heute Abend zu kochen.
exercises.why: Lust haben is one of the fixed verbs that only works with a zu-infinitive, never with a subordinate clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: He finally managed to repair the bicycle.
exercises.german: Er schaffte es endlich, das Fahrrad zu reparieren.
exercises.why: A verb of ability (schaffen) plus a zu-infinitive; the it replaces the usual es-construction and the infinitive closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: Do not forget to take an umbrella.
exercises.german: Vergiss nicht, deinen Schirm mitzunehmen!
exercises.why: The accusative object precedes the prefixed infinitive mitzunehmen, which ends the sentence.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: We plan to move to Berlin next spring.
exercises.german: Wir haben vor, im Frühjahr nach Berlin umzuziehen.
exercises.why: vorhaben is always intransitive and demands a zu-infinitive; the time expression stands in front of it.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: I refuse to talk about it any longer.
exercises.german: Ich weigere mich, darüber weiter zu sprechen.
exercises.why: sich weigern takes a zu-infinitive; the separable verb weiter zu sprechen stands at the very end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: They warned me not to touch the cables.
exercises.german: Sie warnten mich, die Kabel nicht zu berühren.
exercises.why: warnen requires a zu-infinitive with negation, which is placed in front of the final infinitive berühren.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: She hopes to move abroad next year.
exercises.german: Sie hofft, nächstes Jahr ins Ausland zu ziehen.
exercises.why: hoffen is interesting: with a person it takes a dass-clause, but with the intent it takes the zu-infinitive ziehen.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: He denied having lied.
exercises.german: Er bestritt gelogen zu haben.
exercises.why: A verb of denial takes the perfect infinitive without zu, whereas a negated claim would need a dass-clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: She thanked me for helping her.
exercises.german: Sie dankte mir, ihr geholfen zu haben.
exercises.why: A verb of gratitude frames the perfect infinitive with zu between participle and infinitive: geholfen zu haben.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: zu + infinitive instead of a clause
exercises.english: He stopped working when the colleagues arrived.
exercises.german: Er hörte auf zu arbeiten, als die Kollegen kamen.
exercises.why: Two clauses in one sentence: the zu-infinitive after aufhören, then a temporal als-clause with the verb at the end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: He left the house without saying goodbye.
exercises.german: Er verließ das Haus, ohne sich zu verabschieden.
exercises.why: ohne precedes a reflexive object plus zu-infinitive; ohne zu-subject must not appear here.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: She went to bed without eating anything.
exercises.german: Sie ging zu Bett, ohne etwas zu essen.
exercises.why: The accusative object etwas stands in front of zu, and essen is the last word of the infinitive group.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: I am calling you in order to announce my arrival.
exercises.german: Ich rufe dich an, um dir meine Ankunft anzukündigen.
exercises.why: The purpose clause um … zu contains a nominalised object; without a conjunction the infinitive anzukündigen has to be last.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: I get up early in order to catch the first train.
exercises.german: Ich stehe früh auf, um den ersten Zug zu bekommen.
exercises.why: The separable verb in the main clause is split, and the purpose infinitive zu bekommen ends the sentence.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: Do not go out without telling me.
exercises.german: Geh nicht hinaus, ohne mir Bescheid zu sagen.
exercises.why: Negated imperative with an ohne-group: the dative object mir precedes zu sagen, which stands at the end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: Instead of taking the bus, she walked.
exercises.german: Statt mit dem Bus zu fahren, ging sie zu Fuß.
exercises.why: statt … zu replaces a normal verb phrase, the infinitive fahren is preceded by the preparation mit dem Zug-like phrase mit dem Bus.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: Without hesitating, he opened the door.
exercises.german: Ohne zu zögern, öffnete er die Tür.
exercises.why: A fixed idiom of manner: Ohne zu zögern keeps the bare infinitive directly after zu.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: She stopped smoking in order to protect her health.
exercises.german: Sie hörte auf zu rauchen, um ihre Gesundheit zu schützen.
exercises.why: Two infinitive constructions in one sentence: the first ends with rauchen, the purpose group begins with um.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: He is saving money in order to travel around the world.
exercises.german: Er spart Geld, um eine Weltreise zu machen.
exercises.why: Purpose infinitive with an article phrase in front; machen as the last word carries the zu.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: The apology did not stop him from complaining.
exercises.german: Die Entschuldigung hielt ihn nicht davon ab, sich zu beschweren.
exercises.why: davon abhalten is a separable verb whose zu-infinitive must be placed behind the whole main clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: She did it without being asked.
exercises.german: Sie hat es getan, ohne gefragt zu werden.
exercises.why: Passive infinitive with zu: the passive wird is preceded by the Partizip II gefragt and placed at the very end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: He kept talking without noticing the attention of the others.
exercises.german: Er redete weiter, ohne die Aufmerksamkeit der anderen zu bemerken.
exercises.why: The ohne-group is expanded by an accusative phrase; the infinitive bemerken still stands at the very end.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: I need an hour in order to shower.
exercises.german: Ich brauche eine Stunde, um zu duschen.
exercises.why: A separable verb in the purpose group: zu precedes the whole verb, so zu duschen is the last element.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: Instead of complaining, she simply changed providers.
exercises.german: Anstatt sich zu beschweren, hat sie den Anbieter gewechselt.
exercises.why: A perfect main clause may be placed after the anstatt-group; the reflexive sich precedes zu beschweren.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: He left early without saying goodbye to anyone.
exercises.german: Er ging früh, ohne sich von jemandem zu verabschieden.
exercises.why: The prepositional phrase von jemandem separates the reflexive object from zu; verabschieden is last.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: They celebrated the end of the year without buying expensive gifts.
exercises.german: Sie feierten das Jahresende, ohne teure Geschenke zu kaufen.
exercises.why: The adjective phrase teure Geschenke comes before zu; kaufen finishes the infinitive group.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: He took an umbrella along in order to stay dry in the rain.
exercises.german: Er nahm einen Schirm mit, um bei Regen trocken zu bleiben.
exercises.why: Purpose infinitive with a second predicative adjective: zu bleiben closes the sentence.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: I rang twice without reaching you.
exercises.german: Ich habe zweimal angerufen, ohne dich zu erreichen.
exercises.why: Perfect main clause plus an accusative object before the zu-infinitive: dich zu erreichen.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: She is learning Japanese in order to work in Tokyo.
exercises.german: Sie lernt Japanisch, um in Tokio zu arbeiten.
exercises.why: The place expression in Tokio keeps its position between um and the infinitive; arbeiten is verb-final.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: infinitive group with ohne / um / (an)statt ... zu
exercises.english: Without a plan, they wandered through the old town.
exercises.german: Ohne Plan zogen sie durch die Altstadt.
exercises.why: ohne here takes a bare noun instead of a zu-infinitive, which is also possible with this preposition.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The house in which we live is old.
exercises.german: Das Haus, in dem wir wohnen, ist alt.
exercises.why: A prepositional relative clause in dem introduces the verb-final wohnen and is set off by two commas.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The woman whose car was stolen went to the police.
exercises.german: Die Frau, deren Auto gestohlen wurde, ging zur Polizei.
exercises.why: The genitive relative pronoun deren precedes the noun Auto; the passive wurde is verb-final inside the clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: This is the project on which we have been working for months.
exercises.german: Das ist das Projekt, an dem wir seit Monaten arbeiten.
exercises.why: A preposition plus dative an combines with dem into an dem; the two-part verb haben … arbeiten ends the clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The colleague to whom I lent the book has gone on holiday.
exercises.german: Die Kollegin, der ich das Buch geliehen habe, macht gerade Urlaub.
exercises.why: The dative relative pronoun der replaces the prepositional form mit; the perfect form geliehen habe is final.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The hotel in which we stayed was fully booked.
exercises.german: Das Hotel, in dem wir übernachtet haben, war ausgebucht.
exercises.why: in dem as the preposition of location; the perfect verb of the relative clause closes it, while the main clause has its own verb war.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: I know a restaurant where you can eat very well.
exercises.german: Ich kenne ein Restaurant, in dem man sehr gut essen kann.
exercises.why: The preposition in is omitted from the relative pronoun (wo) and reappears as in dem; impersonal man as subject keeps kann last.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: That is the man who, as far as I know, lives next door.
exercises.german: Das ist der Mann, der, soweit ich weiß, nebenan wohnt.
exercises.why: A relative pronoun followed by a comment in brackets; the clause still ends verb-final with wohnt.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The negotiations whose outcome surprised everyone lasted two days.
exercises.german: Die Verhandlungen, deren Ergebnis alle überraschte, dauerten zwei Tage.
exercises.why: The genitive relative clause is inserted in the middle of the sentence and closed by its own finite verb überraschte.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The city in which my parents live is not that big.
exercises.german: Die Stadt, in der meine Eltern wohnen, ist nicht besonders groß.
exercises.why: in der for feminine nouns; the relative pronoun agrees in gender and case with das Haus, in dem.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The house where we used to live has been sold.
exercises.german: Das Haus, da wir früher gewohnt haben, wurde verkauft.
exercises.why: The da-compound is the short variant of the prepositional relative clause: da replaces in dem, the clause stays verb-final.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: We are moving to Leipzig because the flats there are much cheaper.
exercises.german: Wir ziehen nach Leipzig, da die Wohnungen dort viel günstiger sind.
exercises.why: A da-compound in a main-clause position: da points back to Leipzig and replaces weil; the clause ends verb-final with sind.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: She said goodbye yesterday because she is flying to Zurich tomorrow.
exercises.german: Sie hat sich gestern verabschiedet, da sie morgen nach Zürich fliegt.
exercises.why: da as a substitute for the preposition in: it links back to the place just mentioned and precedes a verb-final clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The colleague to whom I told this wants to help us.
exercises.german: Der Kollege, dem ich davon erzählt habe, will uns helfen.
exercises.why: A dative object in front of the reflexive verb; the perfect form erzählt habe is the last element of the relative clause.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The rising electricity prices surprised many households.
exercises.german: Die steigenden Strompreise haben viele Haushalte überrascht.
exercises.why: The present active Partizip I steigenden functions as a predicative attribute before the noun and is declined.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The frozen lake offers a beautiful view.
exercises.german: Der gefrorene See bietet einen schönen Blick.
exercises.why: The Partizip II gefrorene is used passively here because the ice is affected; the ge- prefix is kept with no vowel change.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The injured driver was taken to hospital with serious injuries.
exercises.german: Der verunglückte Fahrer wurde mit schweren Verletzungen ins Krankenhaus gebracht.
exercises.why: A Partizip II as attribute with sein, so there is no ge- prefix; the vowel alternation unglückte is also visible.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The submitted documents will be checked by Friday.
exercises.german: Die eingereichten Unterlagen werden bis Freitag geprüft.
exercises.why: Past Partizip II as attribute: the ge- prefix and the -en ending of eingereichten show passive meaning.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The remote districts that are hard to reach are often ignored.
exercises.german: Die schwer erreichbaren Ortsteile werden oft übersehen.
exercises.why: A Partizip I-like adjective group with zu: the zu-infinitive is embedded inside the attribute before the passive predicate.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The growing distrust towards the administration led to protests.
exercises.german: Das wachsende Misstrauen gegenüber der Verwaltung führte zu Protesten.
exercises.why: Partizip I with a meaning of ongoing development; the prepositional phrase sits between the attribute and the verb.

exercises.skill: Subordinate clauses without a conjunction: relative clause with a preposition, da-compound, participial attribute
exercises.english: The friends with whom we are travelling have known each other since school.
exercises.german: Die Freunde, mit denen wir reisen, kennen sich seit der Schulzeit.
exercises.why: The preposition mit contracts with the relative pronoun to den: mit denen; the main clause keeps its own verb kennen.
